name: Pav Bhaji
cuisine: Mumbai street food (Maharashtra; born around the Girangaon textile mills and the old Cotton Exchange in the 19th century)

ingredients.name: Capsicum, green (shimla mirch)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium capsicum (3 tbsp finely chopped)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ medium onion: 40 g chopped for the bhaji, 15 g chopped raw to serve

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 medium tomato, finely chopped (about ½ cup)

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ cup for the cooker + 2–4 tbsp to adjust the bhaji

ingredients.name: Butter, salted (makhan, e.g. Amul)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 4 tsp in total (10 g cooking, 5 g topping, 5 g for the pav)

equipment: Tawa or wide, flat-bottomed pan (street vendors cook on a huge flat tawa)
Potato masher (the single most useful tool here)
Measuring spoons (a regular teaspoon and tablespoon work)

steps.title: Peel and cube the potato
steps.text: Wash, peel and cut 80 g (1 small) potato into 2 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: Even, pale-cream cubes about the size of a dice
steps.cameraCheck: The potato cubes on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife cutting the peeled potato into cubes.
steps.watchOut: Big uneven chunks stay hard in the middle after cooking; if you see pieces bigger than a thumb joint, cut them again now.

steps.title: Chop the cauliflower
steps.text: Rinse and cut 30 g cauliflower into small florets.
steps.tip: Soak the florets in warm salted water for 2 min if you are worried about small insects, then rinse.
steps.visualCue: 3–4 florets, each about the size of a large grape, no brown spots
steps.cameraCheck: The florets on the board
steps.videoShot: Florets being cut off the stem.
steps.watchOut: Small black specks or insects hide between the florets; if you see any, soak in warm salted water for 2 min and rinse.

steps.title: Dice the carrot
steps.text: Peel and dice 20 g carrot into small pieces.
steps.visualCue: Small orange cubes, about 2 tbsp
steps.cameraCheck: The diced carrot
steps.videoShot: The knife dicing the carrot.
steps.watchOut: Thick carrot pieces stay firm and show up as hard bits in the finished bhaji; keep the dice smaller than the potato.

steps.title: Measure the peas
steps.text: Measure 20 g (2 tbsp) green peas.
steps.visualCue: Bright green peas; frozen peas can go in straight from the freezer
steps.cameraCheck: 2 tbsp peas in a spoon or bowl
steps.videoShot: Peas tumbling into the bowl.
steps.watchOut: Old, wrinkled or grey peas taste dull; if they look like that, use fresh frozen ones.

steps.title: Load the cooker
steps.text: Put the potato, cauliflower, carrot and peas into the pressure cooker. Add 120 ml (½ cup) water and a small pinch (about 0.5 g) of the salt.
steps.visualCue: The water comes about halfway up the vegetables
steps.cameraCheck: The open cooker with vegetables and water
steps.videoShot: Water being poured over the vegetables.
steps.watchOut: Too much water makes a watery bhaji later and too little can scorch the bottom; if the vegetables are not at least half covered, add 2 tbsp more.

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Close the lid and cook on medium heat for 3–4 whistles (about 10–12 min). Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own.
steps.tip: Never force the lid open while there is still pressure.
steps.visualCue: You hear 3–4 whistles; the float valve has dropped before you open the lid
steps.cameraCheck: The closed cooker on the stove
steps.videoShot: Steam puffing as the cooker whistles.
steps.watchOut: Opening the lid while the valve is still up lets hot steam burst out; wait until the valve has dropped and the lid turns easily.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 55 g (½ medium) onion. Keep 40 g for the bhaji and 15 g (1½ tbsp) in a separate small bowl for serving.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces, about the size of a grain of rice
steps.cameraCheck: The 2 small piles of onion
steps.videoShot: The knife chopping the onion fine.
steps.watchOut: Coarse onion pieces stay crunchy in a smooth bhaji; if the pieces are bigger than a pea, chop them again.

steps.title: Chop the capsicum
steps.text: Remove the seeds and finely chop 25 g (¼ medium) capsicum.
steps.visualCue: Small green pieces, about 3 tbsp
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped capsicum
steps.videoShot: The knife dicing capsicum strips.
steps.watchOut: Seeds taste bitter and leave white specks; scrape them out with a spoon before you chop.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Finely chop 75 g (1 medium) tomato.
steps.visualCue: Small, juicy pieces, about ½ cup
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped tomato
steps.videoShot: The knife running through the tomato.
steps.watchOut: Large tomato chunks take much longer to melt into the masala; keep the pieces small so step 17 stays at 4 min.

steps.title: Chop the coriander
steps.text: Finely chop 5 g (1 heaped tbsp) coriander leaves.
steps.visualCue: Fine, fresh green flecks
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped coriander
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through the coriander.
steps.watchOut: Wet leaves turn into a green mush under the knife; pat the leaves dry first.

steps.title: Measure the spices
steps.text: Put a small pinch of turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and 1½ tsp pav bhaji masala together in a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: A small red-brown mound of mixed powders
steps.cameraCheck: The spice bowl
steps.videoShot: Spoons of spice dropping into the bowl.
steps.watchOut: Level teaspoons only; heaped spoons make the bhaji bitter and very hot, and you cannot take spice back out once it is in.

steps.title: Mash the boiled vegetables
steps.text: Open the cooker and mash the vegetables roughly in their cooking water with the masher.
steps.tip: If the potato does not break easily, close the cooker and give it 1 more whistle.
steps.visualCue: A lumpy mash with the water still in it; the potato breaks easily
steps.cameraCheck: The mashed vegetables in the cooker
steps.videoShot: The masher pressing down on the vegetables.
steps.watchOut: Hard lumps in the middle of the potato mean it is undercooked; close the cooker and give it 1 more whistle.

steps.title: Melt the butter
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium heat and add 10 g (2 tsp) butter.
steps.visualCue: The butter melts and foams lightly; it should not brown
steps.cameraCheck: The melted butter on the tawa
steps.videoShot: The butter cube melting and sliding across the tawa.
steps.watchOut: Brown butter and a burnt smell mean the tawa is too hot; lift the tawa off the heat for 10 seconds, then go on at lower heat.

steps.title: Fry the ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Add 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste and stir.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell turns mellow and nutty
steps.cameraCheck: The paste sizzling in the butter
steps.videoShot: The spatula spreading the paste through the butter.
steps.watchOut: Garlic that browns turns bitter within seconds; add the onion at once if it starts to colour.

steps.title: Sauté the onion
steps.text: Add the 40 g chopped onion and stir often.
steps.visualCue: Soft, translucent onion with light golden edges
steps.cameraCheck: The onion on the tawa
steps.videoShot: The spatula turning the onion.
steps.watchOut: Dark brown edges make the bhaji bitter and dull the red colour; if the onion browns fast, sprinkle 1 tbsp water and lower the heat.

steps.title: Sauté the capsicum
steps.text: Add the 25 g chopped capsicum and stir.
steps.visualCue: The capsicum softens and turns a slightly darker green
steps.cameraCheck: The onion-capsicum mix
steps.videoShot: Green pieces being folded through the onion.
steps.watchOut: Capsicum that is still crunchy shows up as green bits in the mash; cook until the pieces bend easily under the spatula.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the 75 g chopped tomato and the rest of the salt (about ¼ tsp). Cook, pressing the tomato with the masher now and then.
steps.visualCue: The tomato breaks down into a thick, glossy pulp with no firm pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The tomato masala on the tawa
steps.videoShot: The masher squashing the tomatoes.
steps.watchOut: Adding the spices before the tomato has melted leaves a sour, raw taste; keep cooking until you see no tomato skin pieces floating in juice.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Tip in the spice bowl (turmeric, chilli powder, pav bhaji masala) and stir. Add 1 tbsp water if it starts to stick.
steps.visualCue: A deep red, fragrant paste; butter starts to glisten at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The red masala on the tawa
steps.videoShot: The spices hitting the masala and turning it red.
steps.watchOut: Dry spices scorch in seconds and smell acrid; if the masala sticks to the tawa, add 1 tbsp water straight away and scrape.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the mashed vegetables with all their cooking water and mix.
steps.visualCue: The pale mash turns orange-red as it mixes with the masala
steps.cameraCheck: The mixed bhaji on the tawa
steps.videoShot: The vegetables sliding out of the cooker onto the masala.
steps.watchOut: Streaks of pale mash mean it is not mixed yet; keep folding until the colour is even.

steps.title: Mash it smooth
steps.text: Mash everything together on the tawa with the masher.
steps.visualCue: A mostly smooth bhaji with only tiny bits of vegetable showing
steps.cameraCheck: The mashed bhaji
steps.videoShot: The masher working in quick up-and-down strokes (the classic street-stall sound).
steps.watchOut: Mashing too gently leaves bits of whole carrot and pea; press down firmly and keep going until only tiny flecks are left.

steps.title: Adjust and simmer
steps.text: Add 2–3 tbsp water if it is too thick, then simmer on low, stirring every minute.
steps.tip: The bhaji thickens as it cools, so stop when it looks slightly looser than you want.
steps.visualCue: Thick but spoonable: it slowly falls off the spatula, like a thick dal, and a little butter shines on the surface
steps.cameraCheck: The spatula lifting some bhaji
steps.videoShot: The bhaji bubbling gently.
steps.watchOut: A watery bhaji will not hold on the pav; simmer 2 min more. A bhaji that sticks and spits is too dry; add 1 tbsp hot water and stir.

steps.title: Finish the bhaji
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the bhaji, add half the coriander, stir and taste for salt.
steps.visualCue: Green flecks through the red bhaji; a sweet, herby smell
steps.cameraCheck: The finished bhaji on the tawa
steps.videoShot: Kasuri methi being crushed over the tawa.
steps.watchOut: Too much kasuri methi tastes bitter; use only ½ tsp, and if the bhaji tastes flat add a tiny pinch of salt rather than more spice.

steps.title: Serve the bhaji
steps.text: Spoon the bhaji into a bowl and put 5 g (1 tsp) butter on top.
steps.visualCue: The butter starts to melt into a shiny pool on top
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl of bhaji with butter
steps.videoShot: The butter melting on the hot bhaji.
steps.watchOut: Leaving the bhaji on the tawa while you toast the pav lets it catch and dry out; move it to the bowl first.

steps.title: Slit the pav
steps.text: Cut 2 pav through the middle horizontally, leaving one edge joined like a book.
steps.visualCue: Each pav opens flat like a book
steps.cameraCheck: The 2 opened pav
steps.videoShot: The knife sliding through a pav.
steps.watchOut: Cutting all the way through leaves two loose halves that are harder to toast; stop about 1 cm before the edge.

steps.title: Make the pav butter
steps.text: Wipe the tawa, put it on medium heat and melt 5 g (1 tsp) butter with a pinch of pav bhaji masala and a pinch of the coriander.
steps.visualCue: Foaming red-flecked butter
steps.cameraCheck: The spiced butter on the tawa
steps.videoShot: The masala swirling into the melted butter.
steps.watchOut: Old bhaji stuck on the tawa burns and makes black specks; wipe the tawa clean first.

steps.title: Toast the pav
steps.text: Press the pav cut-side down into the butter, then flip and toast the outside.
steps.tip: The pav burns fast, so do not walk away.
steps.visualCue: Light golden, crisp cut side, still soft inside
steps.cameraCheck: The toasted cut side of the pav
steps.videoShot: The pav being pressed into the butter and flipped.
steps.watchOut: Pav burns fast and turns hard; if the cut side is dark brown, the heat is too high, so lower it for the next side.

steps.title: Plate it
steps.text: Put the bhaji, 2 pav, the 15 g raw onion, the rest of the coriander and the lemon wedge on a plate.
steps.visualCue: A street-style plate: red bhaji with melting butter, golden pav, white onion, green coriander, yellow lemon
steps.cameraCheck: The full plate
steps.videoShot: A slow pan over the finished plate.
steps.watchOut: Cold pav and cold bhaji taste flat; serve within 2 min of toasting.

reasons: the bhaji itself is a good way to eat 6 vegetables at once (about 300 g raw vegetables, about 10 g fibre in the serving), and nothing is deep-fried. But the dish leans heavily on butter (20 g, about 11 g saturated fat, over half the daily limit), the pav is refined flour, protein is modest (about 14 g) and sodium is high (about 1,250 mg, 63% of the limit). Street and restaurant versions often use 2–3 times as much butter (sometimes margarine or "butter" blends), more potato, more salt and sometimes red food colour.

researchRating.basis: pav bhaji is one of India's most universally loved street foods, and the top home recipes score almost perfectly (search snippets this run: Indian Healthy Recipes (Swasthi's) 4.99 from 744 votes, Hebbar's Kitchen 4.99 from 460 votes and its cooker version 4.96 from 97 votes, Easy Indian Cookbook 5 from 28 votes, Archana's Kitchen cooker version with about 10,890 ratings, value not shown). It stays a little short of 5 because it is widely called heavy or "too buttery" and is seen as an occasional treat rather than everyday food. The rating is unchanged from the 6 Oct version.

storage: The bhaji keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days in an airtight box, and it freezes well for up to 1 month (freeze without the butter topping). Reheat it in a pan with 2–3 tbsp water on low heat, stirring, for 4–5 min (or microwave, covered, for 1.5–2 min, stirring halfway), then add fresh butter, coriander and lemon. Store the pav separately at room temperature (1–2 days) and toast it fresh; pav goes stale in the fridge.
leftoverRemix: Bhaji cheese toastie (or bhaji pulao). Spread 3–4 tbsp cold bhaji on a slice of bread, add chopped onion and a slice of cheese, close with a second slice and toast on a buttered tawa until crisp, 2–3 min per side. Or, for a twist on Mumbai's "tawa pulao", toss 1 cup cooked rice with ½ cup leftover bhaji on a hot tawa for 3 min and finish with lemon and coriander.
burnOff: about 7.5 km of running (524 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 10.5 km of brisk walking (about 2 hr 5 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: wheat pav, onion, garlic and a spice masala blend are all avoided under most vrat rule sets (common rule set assumed)

ekadashi.reason: wheat pav, onion and garlic are commonly avoided on Ekadashi (common rule set assumed; families differ)
